slides.title: UV gets through [[clouds]]
slides.body: Gray skies feel cool and dim, but UV rays still pass through clouds. You don't feel them as heat, so it's easy to skip SPF on cloudy days.

slides.title: Snow and [[windows]]
slides.body: Fresh snow reflects sunlight back up toward your face. And some UV rays come through window glass, so desk and car time near a window adds up.

items.head: Use enough
items.sub: Face, ears, neck and back of hands

items.head: Reapply when you go out
items.sub: Keep a small tube in your bag

items: SPF on, even if it's gray?

caption:
Cloudy winter day? Your SPF still matters ☁️

UV rays pass through clouds, fresh snow reflects light back up, and some UV comes through windows too.
Try three small habits starting tomorrow morning:
Make SPF your last step · Cover ears, neck and hands · Keep a small tube in your bag
